Title: A Chance to Heal

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Ageing MOTHER, SARAH (50s), stirs a pot on the stove as her DAUGHTER, ELLA (20s), enters the kitchen.

SARAH
(looking up)
Ella, my dear. I'm glad you're home.

ELLA
(smiling)
Hi, Mom. I was thinking, maybe we could have a real talk.

SARAH nods, setting down the wooden spoon.

SARAH
Of course. What's on your mind?

ELLA
It's about Dad. I've been thinking a lot about his death, and... I feel like I need to talk to you about something.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Ella and Sarah sit on the old, worn-out couch, sharing a box of tissues.

ELLA
(tearfully)
I've been carrying this anger, this resentment... for so long. I can't keep living like this. I want to forgive him, but I don't know how.

SARAH
(sighs)
Ella, I understand. I feel the same way sometimes. But forgiveness isn't about letting go of your pain or forgetting what happened. It's about recognizing that holding onto that anger only hurts you.

ELLA
(nods)
But how do I do it? How do I let go?

SARAH
You don't have to do it alone. We can do it together. We can write a letter to him. Pour out all your feelings, all the things you wish you could say to him. And then, burn it.

INT. GARAGE - DAY

Ella and Sarah sit on the cold garage floor, surrounded by papers and pens. They write and cry, pouring their hearts out on paper.

ELLA
(tearfully)
I don't know if this is helping, Mom.

SARAH
(reassuringly)
It's okay, Ella. Forgiveness isn't an overnight process. It's a journey. But this is the first step.

INT. BACKYARD - SUNSET

Ella and Sarah stand together, holding hands, as they watch the sun set over the backyard. They light a match and watch as their letters, filled with love, anger, and forgiveness, burn in the fire pit.

ELLA
(sighs)
I feel a little better, Mom.

SARAH
(smiles)
I'm proud of you, Ella. And I'm here for you, always.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Ella and Sarah sit at the kitchen table, drinking tea and enjoying each other's company.

ELLA
(smiling)
Thank you, Mom. For being here for me and helping me through this.

SARAH
(smiling back)
That's what mothers do.

They share a loving smile as the sun pours in through the kitchen window.

FADE OUT.
